chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr ibn Suwayd from Hisham ibn Salim from Sulayman ibn Khalid said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who had much wealth, so he bought goods with it, then stored them, saying: 'This is stored goods; when I wish, I will sell them, and my principal capital will return to me, and more than it.' Is there zakat due on it while it is goods? He said: 'No, until he sells it.' He asked: 'Does he pay for it for what has passed if it is goods?' He said: 'No.'
ai.seo_question: When is zakat due on commercial goods held in inventory?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that commercial goods (matā') are exempt from zakat while held in storage, clarifying that the obligation arises only upon the actual sale. This ruling distinguishes the timing of zakat liability for trade inventory from other asset classes, a key principle in Shia fiqh regarding the purification of wealth through commercial transactions.
